transliteration_key.g: ج (في مصر تُنطق g مثل gate)

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أهلاً يا سامر، معاك لينا
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Lina.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أهلاً يا لينا، إيه الأخبار؟
dialogue.english: Hi Lina, what's new?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله تمام. كلمتك من شوية بس الخط كان مشغول
dialogue.transliteration: el-7amdu lillah tamaam. kallemtak min shwayya bass el-khaTT kaan mashghool
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. I called you a bit ago but the line was busy.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، كنت بكلم أخويا. آسف إني ماعرفتش أرد عليكي
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, kunt bakallem akhuuya. aasef enni ma3rafteesh arudd 3aleeki
dialogue.english: Yeah, I was talking with my brother. Sorry I couldn't answer you.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك. كنت عايزة أكلمك عن الميعاد
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. I wanted to talk to you about the appointment.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: اتفضلي، بس ثانية واحدة، رصيدي هيخلص
dialogue.transliteration: etfaddali, bass saanya wa7da, raseedi hayekhlas
dialogue.english: Go ahead, just a second, my credit is about to run out.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: طيب خليني أقول بسرعة قبل ما الخط يقطع
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb khalleeni 2ool bisor3a 2abl ma el-khaTT ye2Ta3
dialogue.english: Okay, let me say it fast before the call gets cut off.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لأ لأ، خلاص، اتقطع. ممكن تكلميني تاني بعد شوية؟
dialogue.transliteration: la2 la2, khalaas, et2aTa3. mumkin tekalmeeni taani ba3d shwayya?
dialogue.english: No no, that's it, it got cut off. Can you call me back in a bit?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: حاضر، كويس إنك رديت أصلاً. هكلمك تاني
dialogue.transliteration: 7aader, kwayyis ennak radeit aslan. hakallemak taani
dialogue.english: Sure, good that you picked up at all. I'll call you again.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: تسلمي، هستناكي
dialogue.english: Thanks, I'll wait for you.

pair.english: Can you call me back in a bit?

lessons.culture: In Cairo people answer with "ألو" and the caller says who they are with "معاك" plus a name, so "مين معايا؟" is what you ask when you do not know. A call usually opens with a few greetings such as "إزيك، إيه الأخبار" before the point, and jumping straight to business can sound abrupt.

exercises.prompt: You pick up a call from an unknown number. Answer and ask who is calling.

too_formal.item: السلام عليكم، من فضلك من المتصل؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct Arabic, but far more formal than the ordinary way of answering the phone.

exercises.tip: "ألو" opens a call and "مين معايا؟" asks who is on the line.

exercises.prompt: A friend on the phone asks: "إيه الأخبار؟". Say all is fine, thank God.

too_formal.item: الأمور على ما يرام ولله الحمد
too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; a spoken reply is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "الحمد لله" is almost always somewhere in the answer.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ماعرفتش _____ عليك من شوية." Meaning: I couldn't answer you a bit ago.

too_formal.feedback: Understandable, but "رد على" is what people say about answering a call.

exercises.tip: "رد على حد" is the everyday phrase for answering someone's call.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الخط _____ وأنا بكلمك." Meaning: The call got cut off while I was talking to you.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a technical report, not something said on the phone.

exercises.tip: "اتقطع" is the everyday word for a dropped call.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "My battery died."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but far more formal than how people actually say it.

exercises.tip: "فصل" is what a phone does when its battery dies.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There's no signal here."

too_formal.item: لا توجد تغطية شبكية في هذا المكان
too_formal.feedback: Correct but reads like a technician's report, not spoken Egyptian.

exercises.tip: "مفيش" means "there isn't" and "شبكة" is the network signal.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "My credit ran out"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "خلص" is the everyday word, not "انتهى".

exercises.tip: "رصيد" is prepaid phone credit.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to answer an incoming call?

too_formal.feedback: Too formal; nobody opens a phone call this way in Cairo.

exercises.tip: "ألو" answers the phone; the other phrases come once the call is going.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "مشغول / كان / الخط".

too_formal.feedback: That would be an unusual, technical way to say the line was busy.

exercises.tip: "الخط" comes right after "كان" here.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "شوية / بعد / تكلمني / تاني / ممكن".

too_formal.item: هل بإمكانك معاودة الاتصال بي لاحقاً
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but the formal written version, not the spoken order.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" opens the request, and "تاني" means "again".

reply.english: In front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: لينا، نتقابل فين بكرة؟
dialogue.english: Lina, where should we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: إيه رأيك نتقابل في الكافيه اللي قدام الجامعة؟
dialogue.transliteration: eh ra2yak net2aabel fil-kaafeeh elli 2eddaam el-gaam3a?
dialogue.english: What do you think, shall we meet at the cafe in front of the university?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: فكرة حلوة. الساعة كام تنفع معاكي؟
dialogue.english: Good idea. What time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: طيب فين بالظبط، قدام الكافيه؟
dialogue.english: Okay, where exactly, in front of the cafe?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، هقابلك قدام البوابة الرئيسية
dialogue.english: Yes, I'll meet you in front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: تمام، أنا هبقى هناك قبلك أكيد
dialogue.english: Great, I'll definitely be there before you.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ماتتأخريش عليا يا لينا
dialogue.english: Don't be late on me, Lina.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك، ولو اتأخرت هكلمك
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhemmak, we law et2akharet hakallemak
dialogue.english: Don't worry, and if I'm late I'll call you.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ماشي، نشوف بعض بكرة
dialogue.english: Okay, see you tomorrow.

response.english: In front of the main entrance.

pair.english: What do you think, shall we go together?

lessons.culture: In Cairo people usually meet at a cafe or give a landmark such as a mosque or a metro station instead of a street address. Being a few minutes late is common, so a quick call to say you are on your way is normal and not rude.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks you: "نتقابل فين؟". Suggest meeting at the cafe.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct, but far more formal than a casual suggestion.

exercises.tip: "خلينا" plus a verb is the everyday way to suggest doing something together.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "الساعة كام تنفع معاك؟". Say that 7 o'clock works.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but sounds like a written appointment confirmation, not spoken.

exercises.tip: "تنفع" is how a time "works" in Egyptian speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "هقابلك _____ البوابة الرئيسية." Meaning: I'll meet you in front of the main entrance.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but "قدام" is what is actually said, not "أمام".

exercises.tip: "قدام" means "in front of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "لو _____ كلمني." Meaning: If you're late, call me.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but very formal written Arabic, not how it is said.

exercises.tip: "لو" plus a past-tense verb is the everyday "if".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "Don't be late."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a formal written notice, not spoken Egyptian.

exercises.tip: "ما" before the verb and "ش" after it makes the everyday negative command.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I'll be there before you."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically the same, but it uses the formal "سـ" instead of the spoken "ha".

exercises.tip: "ha" plus a verb makes the everyday future in Cairene speech.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "What time suits you?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiffer than the everyday spoken question.

exercises.tip: "كام" means "what number", so "الساعة كام" is "what time".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's meet at the cafe"?

too_formal.feedback: A correct classical form, but not how it is said in conversation.

exercises.tip: "خلينا" plus a verb is the everyday "let's".

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "تنفع / الساعة / سبعة".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more elaborate than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: The time comes first, then "تنفع" at the end.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الرئيسية / البوابة / قدام / هقابلك".

too_formal.item: سألتقي بك أمام المدخل الرئيسي للمبنى
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a much longer, written-style sentence.

exercises.tip: "هقابلك" (I'll meet you) opens the sentence, then the place.

phrases.arabic: خَلِينَا نْشُوف يُوم يِنَاسِبْنَا إِحْنَا الاِتْنِين
phrases.transliteration: khalleena nshoof yoom yenaasebna e7na l-etneen

phrases.arabic: يِنْفَع نِتْقَابِل بَعْد الضُّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح؟
phrases.transliteration: yenfa3 net2aabel ba3d ed-dohr badal es-subh?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ألو سامر، عايزة أغير ميعادنا النهارده
dialogue.english: Hello Samer, I want to change our appointment today.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: في إيه؟ حصل حاجة؟
dialogue.english: What happened? Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، حصلتلي ظروف في البيت ومش هقدر آجي النهارده
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, 7asalitli zuroof fil-beit we mish ha2dar aagi en-nahaarda
dialogue.english: Yeah, something came up at home and I can't come today.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك. ينفع نأجل لبكرة؟
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. Can we postpone to tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: مفيش مشكلة، نأجل لبكرة. بس ينفع نتقابل بعد الضهر بدل الصبح؟
dialogue.transliteration: mafeesh mushkila, ne2aggel le-bukra. bass yenfa3 net2aabel ba3d ed-dohr badal es-subh?
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to tomorrow. But can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بعد الضهر أحسن ليا كمان
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, ba3d ed-dohr a7san leyya kamaan
dialogue.english: Great, the afternoon is better for me too.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: تسلم، معلش، آسفة إني غيرت فجأة
dialogue.transliteration: teslem, ma3lesh, aasfa enni ghayyart fag2a
dialogue.english: Thanks, sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك، بيحصل. المكان لسه نفس المكان؟
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhemmak, biye7sal. el-makaan lessa nafs el-makaan?
dialogue.english: Don't worry, it happens. Is the place still the same place?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: لأ، غيرنا المكان، هنتقابل في الكافيه الجديد
dialogue.transliteration: la2, ghayyarna el-makaan, hanet2aabel fil-kaafeeh el-gedeed
dialogue.english: No, we changed the place, we'll meet at the new cafe.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: ماشي، هحفظ العنوان. شكراً إنك قلتيلي بدري
dialogue.transliteration: maashi, ha7faz el-3enwaan. shukran ennik 2olteeli badri
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll save the address. Thanks for telling me early.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: العفو، هشوفك بكرة بعد الضهر
dialogue.english: You're welcome, see you tomorrow afternoon.

pair.english: I want to change the appointment.

pair.arabic: يِنْفَع نِتْقَابِل بَعْد الضُّهْر بِدَل الصُّبْح؟
pair.transliteration: yenfa3 net2aabel ba3d ed-dohr badal es-subh?
pair.english: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

response.english: Yes, the afternoon is better for me.

pair.english: Is the place still the same place?

lessons.culture: Plans shift often in Cairo, and changing one is accepted when you say "معلش" and give a short reason such as "ظروف" without going into details. The other person usually answers "ولا يهمك" or "عادي".

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: "معلش، آسف إني غيرت فجأة". Tell them not to worry about it.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the short spoken reassurance.

exercises.tip: "ولا يهمك" and "عادي" are the standard easy ways to say "don't worry".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "ينفع نأجل لبكرة؟". Agree, saying no problem.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but this is the written, not the spoken, register.

exercises.tip: "مفيش مشكلة" is a very common easy agreement.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ ظروف ومش هقدر آجي." Meaning: Something came up for me and I can't come.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; the spoken version is much shorter.

exercises.tip: "حصلتلي ظروف" is the fixed everyday phrase for "something came up".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ينفع نتقابل بعد الضهر _____ الصبح؟" Meaning: Can we meet in the afternoon instead of the morning?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal than the short spoken "بدل".

exercises.tip: "بدل" means "instead of" in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "I can't come today."

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but more formal than the everyday spoken phrase.

exercises.tip: "النهارده" is "today" and "مش هقدر" is "I won't be able to".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Can we postpone to tomorrow?"

too_formal.item: هل يمكننا تأجيل الموعد إلى الغد؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct but a longer, written-style question.

exercises.tip: "ينفع" plus a verb is the everyday way to ask "can we...".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Is the place still the same place?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but more formal phrasing than the spoken question.

exercises.tip: "لسه" means "still" in everyday Cairene speech.

exercises.prompt: Which is a natural apology for changing plans suddenly?

too_formal.item: أعتذر منكم عن هذا التغيير الطارئ
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but stiff and overly formal for a friend.

exercises.tip: "معلش" softens an apology; "آسف" is a man and "آسفة" a woman.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "لبكرة / نأجل / ينفع".

too_formal.item: هل من الممكن أن نؤجل الأمر إلى الغد
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a much longer formal question.

exercises.tip: "ينفع" opens the question, then the verb, then the day.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "الصبح / بدل / بعد الضهر / نتقابل / ينفع".
exercises.answer: ينفع نتقابل بعد الضهر بدل الصبح
accepted: ينفع نتقابل بعد الضهر بدل الصبح
ممكن نتقابل بعد الضهر بدل الصبح
yenfa3 net2aabel ba3d ed-dohr badal es-subh

too_formal.item: هل بإمكاننا اللقاء بعد الظهيرة عوضاً عن الصباح؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer, more formal question.

exercises.tip: "ينفع" opens it, then the verb, then the two times being compared.

reply.english: Sure, what should I tell him?

phrases.english: Can you pass him a message from me?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: لأ، مش هنا دلوقتي، نزل السوق
dialogue.transliteration: la2, mish hena delwa2ti, nizil es-soo2
dialogue.english: No, he's not here right now, he went out to the market.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: آه، هيرجع إمتى تقريباً؟
dialogue.english: Ah, roughly when will he be back?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: معرفش بالظبط، كمان شوية إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: ma3rafsh bezzabt, kamaan shwayya in shaa2 allaah
dialogue.english: I don't know exactly, in a bit God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: طيب ممكن تبلغه رسالة مني؟
dialogue.english: Okay, can you take a message for me?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: قوليله إن رامي اتصل وعايزه يكلمني
dialogue.english: Tell him Rami called and wants him to call me.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: طيب، هقوله أول ما يوصل
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: هو معاه رقمي؟
dialogue.english: Does he have my number?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: معرفش، خليني آخد رقمك احتياطي
dialogue.english: I don't know, let me take your number just in case.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: اتفضلي، شكراً أوي على المعروف
dialogue.english: Here you go, thanks a lot for the favor.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: العفو، وهبلغه الخبر أول ما يدخل
dialogue.transliteration: el-3afw, we haballaghu el-khabar awwel ma yedkhul
dialogue.english: You're welcome, and I'll pass him the news as soon as he's in.

response.english: No, he's not here right now.
I don't know exactly, in a bit.

pair.english: Can you take a message for me?

response.english: Sure, what should I tell him?

lessons.culture: In Cairo a family member or flatmate will usually pick up for someone who is out and pass on the message, so callers give their name clearly at the start. "شكراً أوي" is the common thanks for a favor, and "العفو" or "ولا يهمك" is the reply.

exercises.prompt: A caller asks: "سامر موجود؟" but he is out. Say he's not here right now.

too_formal.item: لا، إنه غير متواجد في الوقت الحالي
too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but sounds like an office receptionist, not a spoken reply.

exercises.tip: "مش هنا دلوقتي" is the everyday "not here right now".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "ممكن تبلغه رسالة مني؟". Agree and ask what to tell him.

too_formal.item: بالتأكيد، ما الذي تريد أن أخبره به؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the everyday phrasing.

exercises.tip: "أقوله إيه؟" is the natural way to ask what to relay.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ يكلمني." Meaning: Tell him to call me.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically correct but a written-style instruction, not the short spoken one.

exercises.tip: "قوله" is the short spoken form of "tell him".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "هقوله _____ ما يوصل." Meaning: I'll tell him as soon as he arrives.

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a more formal written order of the sentence.

exercises.tip: "أول ما" is the everyday way to say "as soon as".

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian Arabic: "Do you have my number?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but more formal wording than the short spoken question.

exercises.tip: "معاك" and "عندك" both work for "do you have" here.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Thanks a lot."

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but far more formal than the everyday "شكراً أوي".

exercises.tip: "أوي" after a word means "very" in Egyptian.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "When will he be back?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but it uses the formal "متى" instead of the spoken "إمتى".

exercises.tip: "إمتى" is the everyday word for "when".

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural reply to "شكراً أوي"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a more formal set phrase than the everyday reply.

exercises.tip: "العفو" is the standard easy reply to a thank-you.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "رسالة / تبلغه / ممكن / مني".

too_formal.item: هل يمكن أن تدون له رسالة؟
too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer, more formal question.

exercises.tip: "ممكن" opens the request, then the verb, then what is asked for.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in a natural order: "يوصل / ما / أول / هقوله".

too_formal.feedback: Correct meaning, but a longer written-style sentence.

exercises.tip: "هقوله" (I'll tell him) opens it, then the time clause "أول ما يوصل".

reply.english: No, I haven't read it yet.
Sure, as soon as I arrive.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: لأ، ما شفتش رسالتك. مفيش شبكة هنا والإنترنت ضعيف
dialogue.transliteration: la2, ma shoftesh resaltak. mafeesh shabaka hena wel-enternet Da3eef
dialogue.english: No, I didn't see your message. There's no signal here and the internet is weak.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: يمكن الرسالة ما اتبعتتش. هبعتهالك تاني
dialogue.transliteration: yemken er-resaala ma etba3atetsh. hab3at-haalak taani
dialogue.english: Maybe the message wasn't sent. I'll send it to you again.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: ماشي. وابعتلي الموقع كمان
dialogue.english: Okay. And send me the location too.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: حاضر، وهبعتلك فويس أشرحلك الطريق
dialogue.english: Sure, and I'll send you a voice message explaining the way.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: ماشي، هبعتها على الجروب
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll send it on the group.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: البطارية خلصت تقريبًا، هشحن الموبايل وأرد عليك
dialogue.transliteration: el-baTTareyya khelSet ta2reeban, hash7an el-mobaayl w arodd 3aleek
dialogue.english: My battery's almost dead, I'll charge my phone and reply to you.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: تمام. ولو النت فصل؟
dialogue.english: Great. And if the internet cuts out?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: ما تقلقش، هكتبلك على التطبيق أول ما ألاقي شبكة
dialogue.transliteration: ma t2la2sh, hakteblak 3at-taTbee2 awwel ma la2i shabaka
dialogue.english: Don't worry, I'll write to you on the app as soon as I find a signal.

response.english: Yes, I received it this morning.

pair.english: Why didn't you reply to me?

response.english: I didn't see your message, sorry.

pair.english: Will you write to me when you arrive?

response.english: Of course, I'll write to you on the app.

pair.english: Did you hear the voice message?

lessons.culture: Many Egyptians send voice notes, called فويس, rather than typing, and say لوكيشن for a shared location. Friends type Egyptian in Arabic letters or in "Franco", Latin letters with numbers such as 3 for ع and 7 for ح, while formal messages to work or a teacher are kept more careful.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "رسالتي وصلتلك؟". Say yes, it just arrived.

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; "لسه" is the spoken "just".

exercises.tip: "لسه" before a participle means it has just happened.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "قريت رسالتي؟". Say no, you haven't read it yet.

too_formal.feedback: "لم" is written; spoken Egyptian wraps the verb in ما…ش.

exercises.tip: ما…ش wraps the verb: ما قريتهاش = I didn't read it.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "ما _____ رسالتك" (I didn't see your message.)

too_formal.feedback: "لم أر" is written Arabic; Cairo says "ما شفتش".

exercises.tip: The final ش is part of the negation ما…ش.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "النت _____" (The internet is weak.)
exercises.tip: "النت" is everyday Egyptian for الإنترنت.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian: "Send me a photo." (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: "أرسل" is written; Egyptians say "ابعت".

exercises.tip: To a woman: ابعتيلي صورة.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian: "The message wasn't sent."

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; spoken Egyptian uses ما…ش and "اتبعتت".

exercises.tip: "اتبعت" = was sent.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I'll send a voice message"?
exercises.tip: "فويس" is what people say; the full word is رسالة صوتية.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks "Did you read my message?"

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; Egyptians drop هل and say "قريت".

exercises.tip: A question in Egyptian is often just a statement with a rising voice.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "توصل / اكتبلي / لما"

too_formal.feedback: "عندما" is written; Egyptians say "لما".

exercises.tip: "لما" = when.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "بعدين / هرد / عليك"

too_formal.feedback: "لاحقًا" is written; Egyptians say "بعدين".

exercises.tip: "بعدين" = later.

reply.english: Of course, I'll send you the link.
Yes, I can see you well.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: اللينك وصل. شغل الكاميرا لو سمحت
dialogue.transliteration: el-link weSel. shaghghal el-kamera law sama7t
dialogue.english: The link arrived. Turn on the camera, please.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: أيوه، الصورة واضحة، بس مش سامعك
dialogue.transliteration: aywa, eS-Soora waD7a, bas mesh sam3ak
dialogue.english: Yes, the picture is clear, but I can't hear you.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: استنى، هلبس السماعة. سامعني كويس دلوقتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: estanna, halbes es-sammaa3a. sam3eni kwayyes delwa2ti?
dialogue.english: Wait, I'll put on my headphones. Can you hear me well now?

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: أهو، دلوقتي الصوت واضح
dialogue.english: There, now the sound is clear.

dialogue.speaker: Khaled
dialogue.arabic: تمام. وطفي المايك لما ما تتكلمش، فيه دوشة عندك
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. w Taffi el-mayk lamma ma tetkallemsh, feeh dawsha 3andak
dialogue.english: Great. And turn off the mic when you're not talking, there's noise at your end.

pair.english: Can we do a video call?

response.english: Yes, I can see you well.
Wait, I'll move closer to the router.

lessons.culture: Video calls keep Cairo families close to relatives working in the Gulf or abroad, and a call opens with greetings and إزيك before anyone fixes the sound. Egyptians borrow English tech words freely: لينك, مايك, شير, and هنّج (from "hang") for a frozen screen.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "ممكن نعمل مكالمة فيديو؟". Agree and say you'll send the link.

too_formal.feedback: "سأرسل" and "الرابط" are written; Egyptians say "هبعتلك اللينك".

exercises.tip: To a woman: هبعتلِك اللينك (hab3atlek).

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "سامعني كويس؟". Say no, the sound is choppy.

too_formal.feedback: "متقطع" is written; Egyptians say "بيقطع".

exercises.tip: "بيقطع" = keeps cutting out.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "سامعني _____؟" (Can you hear me well?)

too_formal.feedback: "جيدًا" is written Arabic; Cairo says "كويس".

exercises.tip: "كويس" = well / good.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "مش _____" (I can't hear you.) (a man speaking)

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; Egyptians say "مش سامعك".

exercises.tip: A woman says: مش سامعاك.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian: "Can you see me?" (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; Egyptians use the participle "شايفني".

exercises.tip: To a woman: شايفاني؟

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian: "I'll move closer to the router."

too_formal.feedback: "سأقترب" is written; Egyptians say "هقرب".

exercises.tip: "هـ" before the verb marks the future.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "The sound is choppy"?
exercises.tip: "هنجت" = froze, said of a screen or a phone.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Turn on the camera"? (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: Nobody says "آلة التصوير"; it is "الكاميرا".

exercises.tip: To a woman: شغلي الكاميرا.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "تاني / هخرج / وأدخل"

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; "تاني" is the spoken "again".

exercises.tip: "تاني" = again.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "الشاشة / أشارك / خليني"

too_formal.feedback: "دعني" is written; Egyptians say "خليني".

exercises.tip: "خليني" = let me.

challenge.title: A Phone Call to Rearrange Plans
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a phone conversation of at least 10 lines. It must include answering the phone, proposing a place and a time to meet, changing that plan for a real reason, agreeing on a new time or place, and, if the person you called is not free, leaving a message for someone else to pass on.
required_elements: Saying who is calling, using مين معايا or معاك plus a name.
A suggestion of where to meet, using خلينا نتقابل or a similar phrase.
A question about time, using الساعة كام تنفع or a similar phrase.
A reason for changing the plan, using حصلتلي ظروف or a similar phrase.
A request to postpone or change, using ينفع نأجل or ينفع نتقابل.
An apology for the change, using معلش، آسف or a similar phrase.
A reassurance in response, using ولا يهمك.
A closing thank-you, using شكراً أوي or تسلم.
At least one exchange about leaving or taking a message, using رسالة, قوله, or بلغه.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أَلّو؟
dialogue.english: Hello?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: أهلاً يا سامر، معاك لينا. إيه الأخبار؟
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan ya saamer, ma3aak leena. eh el-akhbaar?
dialogue.english: Hi Samer, it's Lina. What's new?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله تمام. في إيه؟
dialogue.english: All good, thank God. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: خلينا نتقابل في الكافيه بكرة، الساعة كام تنفع معاك؟
dialogue.transliteration: khalleena net2aabel fil-kaafeeh bukra, es-saa3a kaam tenfa3 ma3aak?
dialogue.english: Let's meet at the cafe tomorrow, what time suits you?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: الساعة خمسة تنفع
dialogue.english: 5 o'clock works.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: تمام، هقابلك قدام البوابة الرئيسية
dialogue.english: Great, I'll meet you in front of the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: آسف، حصلتلي ظروف في البيت ومش هقدر آجي الساعة خمسة
dialogue.transliteration: aasef, 7asalitli zuroof fil-beit we mish ha2dar aagi es-saa3a khamsa
dialogue.english: Sorry, something came up at home and I can't come at 5.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك. ينفع نأجل لسبعة؟
dialogue.english: Don't worry about it. Can we postpone to 7?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: مفيش مشكلة، نأجل لسبعة. معلش، آسف إني غيرت فجأة
dialogue.transliteration: mafeesh mushkila, ne2aggel le-sab3a. ma3lesh, aasef enni ghayyart fag2a
dialogue.english: No problem, we'll postpone to 7. Sorry for the sudden change.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمك خالص. ولو مش هتعرف تيجي، ممكن أسيب رسالة مع أخوك؟
dialogue.transliteration: wala yhemmak khaales. we law mish hate3raf teegi, mumkin aseeb resaala ma3a akhuuk?
dialogue.english: Don't worry at all. And if you can't come, can I leave a message with your brother?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أكيد، هقوله. شكراً أوي على صبرك
dialogue.english: Sure, I'll tell him. Thanks a lot for your patience.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.arabic: العفو، هشوفك الساعة سبعة
dialogue.english: You're welcome, see you at 7.
